rows.source: TrueHD object-presentation channels / JOC reconstructed object signals
rows.damf: CAF 24-bit BE, one channel per element
rows.adm: `data` chunk 24-bit LE, one track per element
rows.classification: sample-exact
rows.note: 590 of 590 declared DAMF/ADM track pairs are sample-identical (SHA-256 of the samples equal) over 25 inputs including the whole-film Pi (242322080 frames); the full pairing matrix confirms every declared pair (True). The ADM carries exactly the PCM the decoder produced; JOC objects are the decoder's reconstruction, not the master (differential claim).

rows.internal: bed slots, conformed to 7.1.2 by default
rows.adm: DirectSpeakers tracks first, `RC_*` labels
rows.classification: label-confirmed
rows.note: LFE is sample-identical in every input; harness C21 codes the bed as Rss, Lss, LFE and the tones land under the matching labels with conform on ([None, None, None, 100.0, 600.0, 500.0, None, None, None, None, 440.0]) and off. LFE is identified only by the `RC_LFE` label and position [-1,1,-1] (profile table 10); a BS.2127 renderer does not recognise that label (EAR warning) - a profile-level interoperability limit shared with Dolby's own files.

rows.source: element order: beds, ISF, dynamic objects
rows.adm: `chna` -> ATU -> AT -> AS -> AC chain
rows.note: Every chna entry resolves through a unique UID/track/stream/channel chain to the audioObject that owns it; no dangling, duplicate or orphan node in any file (25 inputs, 0 findings on the whole film).

rows.adm: 1:1 for beds and dynamic objects; ISF absent
rows.classification: ISF dropped silently (see ISF row)
rows.note: Bed, dynamic-object and total element counts agree between OAMD, DAMF and ADM on every input (all corpus beds are LFE-only). Codec channels, JOC reconstructed signals, OAMD programme objects and ADM audioObjects are counted separately in the report.

rows.adm: `Atmos_Obj_k` / `AO_100b+`, one channel format per object
rows.note: No object changes track or id through any programme: block tiling is gapless and sorted for every object (gaps 0, overlaps 0 on real material), and the PCM under each object's channel format is identical to the DAMF element from first to last sample.

rows.adm: `position X/Y`, 10 decimals
rows.note: 0 value mismatches at float32 precision over 36434 matched events; against the raw OAMD dump the mapping holds within 9.7e-05 (the dump's 4 decimals) on 6 TrueHD clips. No axis swap, inversion, offset or clamp.

rows.adm: `position Z`, omitted when 0 (profile)
rows.classification: omission = 0 per profile table 11
rows.note: Absent Z is read as 0.0 by the profile rule; the comparator keeps presence separate from value and found no mismatch.

rows.adm: none (profile forbids `absoluteDistance`; cartesian blocks)
rows.classification: parsed but discarded; not representable in DAMF or in the profile; corpus never specifies it
rows.note: Harness C19 pushes distance 2.0 and infinity through `Timeline::push`: nothing reaches DAMF or ADM and nothing is reported. The corpus carries `unspecified` only, so no real scene loses information today.

rows.adm: omitted on active objects; `0.0` + importance `0` on inactive
rows.classification: avoidable loss: the profile text forbids it, Dolby's converters write it anyway
rows.note: Harness C02: -6 dB, +3 dB, -inf and a mid-stream -12 dB change are all lost in oadec's ADM (3 losses, the change popped) while the PCM is unscaled - a muted active object becomes audible. Dolby's Conversion Tool and DEE write `<gain>` (linear) on 4 active blocks for the same DAMF and emit a block for the gain change. On real material every gain is 0 dB, so no decoded stream is affected today.

rows.adm: `width`=`depth`=`height`
rows.classification: uniform size preserved; Dolby writes the same triple (+`diffuse 1`)
rows.note: Uniform sizes 0.25/0.5/1.0 round-trip exactly in both oadec's and Dolby's ADM. The corpus never carries a non-zero size.

rows.adm: three identical values (profile table 11 requires identical values)
rows.classification: collapse happens in the programme model, before both writers; the selected axis is an implementation choice; neither DAMF nor the profile can carry three axes
rows.note: Harness C04 pushes size [0.2, 0.5, 0.8] through `Timeline::push`: DAMF and ADM carry only the first axis (DAMF sizes per object: object 1: [0.2]; object 2: [0.5]), silently. Not representable downstream, but the choice of axis (first, not max or mean) and the silence are oadec's.

rows.adm: none (profile: `objectDivergence` shall not be used)
rows.classification: not representable in DAMF or the profile; no corpus stream carries it
rows.note: No test material exists and the authoring route cannot produce it; N/T, not PASS.

rows.adm: omitted on active objects (profile), `0` on inactive
rows.classification: profile rule; Dolby drops it identically; corpus always 1.0
rows.note: Harness C03 (importance 0.5 and 0.0 on active objects): 2 losses in oadec's ADM; Dolby's converter writes importance on 0 blocks for the same stimulus. Absent importance means 10 (BS.2076 default) = full priority, which equals the corpus value 1.0.

rows.source: OAMD: linear ramp from the update time (TS 103 420 5.6.2)
rows.adm: `jumpPosition=1` always (profile)
rows.classification: same shape (ramp starting at the event) on both sides
rows.note: BS.2076-3 section 9.3 and TS 103 420 figure 4 describe the same start-anchored ramp; the profile's `jumpPosition=1` is the right mode. The evaluator's self-check returns 0 against a synthetic ADM carrying the real ramps.

rows.adm: fixed: 0 on block 1, 250 samples afterwards (`INTERPOLATION_SAMPLES`)
rows.classification: profile rule (table 11 mandates 0 then 250); Dolby's converters write the same and Dolby's reader ignores any value; loss measured
rows.note: 36158 of the matched real-material blocks carry 250 where the DAMF ramp was 1536 (or 32/1152/1472). Dolby's Conversion Tool and DEE write {'0': 8, '250': 3278} for a stimulus cycling 0/32/250/480/1536/2048; every read-back through the Conversion Tool - of oadec's ADM, of a real-ramp variant and of Dolby's own ADM - returns rampLength 0 ({'0': 128}). Metadata-domain deviation up to 1.67 room units within one block per event; rendered by EAR the fixed ramp costs, against a real-ramp variant of the same file, fast-thd: 6.9-17.4 dB; pihead: 36.5-63.0 dB (min SDR per layout), while oadec and Dolby render bit-identically (7/7 layout comparisons).

rows.adm: `rtime` hh:mm:ss.fffff (10 us), `duration` rounded independently
rows.classification: sample-exact recovery
rows.note: Every ADM rtime decodes (nearest sample) to the DAMF samplePos: 0 time mismatches on 25 inputs incl. the whole film (30576 matched, 0 defects). 0 of 73014 timecodes fail to re-encode to the identical string. Blocks tile without gaps in the sample domain; rtime and duration are rounded independently (10-us `tile_dec` histogram all 0 on real material).

rows.adm: kept
rows.note: Against oadec's raw OAMD dump: 711 DAMF states and 694 ADM blocks fall exactly on OAMD update times (0 / 0 do not); 80 ADM blocks sit on times that only exist with the +32 term (21506 updates in the clips carry block_offset_factor 1).

rows.adm: block 1 at 00:00:00.00000 (profile); synthetic when the first event is later
rows.classification: corner case: real material always starts at 0; when it does not, oadec holds the first state from 0 and drops the real event (time lost), Dolby writes a default (0,0,0) block then the real event
rows.note: Harness C06: {'bed_event': 1, 'synthetic_block0': 2, 'absorbed_by_synthetic': 2}. Both behaviours invent something for a span DAMF leaves undefined; oadec's loses the arrival time of the first state. Not observed on any decoded stream.

rows.adm: last block ends at `frames`; audioProgramme end = frames
rows.classification: one writer defect on synthetic input (Q): a block can run past the programme end
rows.note: Real material: last block ends at the programme end for every object (True), programme span = frames, DAMF frames = ADM frames. Harness C07: an event past the end is dropped (fine) but the preceding block's duration is computed from it and overruns the end (1 object).

rows.adm: one block per event minus popped/superseded, plus synthetic
rows.classification: ledger identity holds; ramp-only changes become duplicate blocks or are popped
rows.note: `adm_blocks = states - superseded - beyond_end - trailing_popped - absorbed + synthetic` holds on every input. 73 duplicate blocks and 59 trailing pops on real material, all ramp-only changes the profile cannot express. No coalescing, resampling or rate limiting.

rows.adm: `Slot::None` - audio and metadata dropped
rows.classification: silent drop; no diagnostic; no corpus stream carries ISF (N/T on real material)
rows.note: Harness C13 (4 ISF objects between the bed and 2 objects): the ISF tones appear in no output track ([None, None, None, 100.0, None, None, None, None, None, None, 440.0, 880.0]) and no warning is printed. On real material N/T; at the writer level a silent loss.

rows.adm: none (profile: DirectSpeakers blocks have no rtime/duration)
rows.classification: profile rule; Dolby's converters drop them identically; corpus beds never change
rows.note: Harness C05: 2 bed changes lost, LFE PCM unscaled; Dolby drops the same (S8, static bed gain -6 dB also ignored). 0 bed changes lost on real material - none, because the LFE beds never change.

rows.adm: `RC_*` labels + table-10 positions; other channels refused
rows.classification: beds beyond 7.1.2 make `AdmWriter::create` fail explicitly (good), `Ls/Rs` of a 5.1 bed are labelled as side surrounds (untested on real material: all corpus beds are LFE-only)
rows.note: C14: `create: bed channel Tfl is not allowed in a Dolby Atmos master ADM bed` - an explicit failure, not a silent file. Zone rectangles equal the profile tables ([] findings). The LFE-only conformed bed passes every profile rule; with `--no-bed-conform` the LFE-only set is not one of table 16's configuration sets - and neither is Dolby's own output for the same DAMF.

rows.adm: objects start below `AO_100b` when the bed has fewer than 10 channels
rows.classification: profile table 17 violation; Dolby numbers objects from `AO_100b` regardless of bed size
rows.note: C11 (no bed): ['profile-id', 'profile-id']. The default 7.1.2 conform yields `AO_100b` and is clean; any smaller bed with conform off is not. Semantically harmless; structurally out of profile.

rows.adm: `audioTrackUID sampleRate` = stream rate; 250-sample constant scaled
rows.classification: profile requires 48000 (table 23); a 96 kHz or 44.1 kHz programme is written without a warning
rows.note: C15 (96 kHz): file written, interpolationLength 0.002604 s = 250 samples, findings ['profile-sample-rate', 'profile-sample-rate']. No Atmos material at 96 kHz exists in the library; the 44.1 kHz Pi encode is the only real case (N/T for decoded output beyond the writer).

rows.adm: APR_1001 -> ACO_1001 -> AO_1001 (bed) + AO_100b.. (objects); custom DirectSpeakers pack AP_00011001; one Objects pack per object
rows.classification: identical element inventory and ids to Dolby's converters on the same DAMF
rows.note: Every produced ADM passes the reference-graph, chna and profile checks with zero findings (default conform).

rows.adm: one UID per PCM track; chna numTracks = numUIDs = channels
rows.note: Chain verified on every file; the negative controls show a dangling trackRef and a wrong UID sample rate are caught.

rows.adm: ebuCore 2016 namespace, BS.2076-1 timecodes
rows.classification: well-formed, references complete, profile-conformant; the profile's audioStreamFormat double reference makes strict BS.2076 readers (EAR) refuse the file - Dolby's own files included
rows.note: EAR renders only after the pack reference is removed from audioStreamFormat (applied identically to oadec's and Dolby's files); with that edit oadec and Dolby render bit-identically.

rows.adm: `RF64` FourCC, ds64 riffSize/dataSize/sampleCount, `fmt` tag 1 (24-bit), data, axml, chna, dbmd
rows.classification: RF64 (EBU Tech 3306) rather than the BS.2088 `BW64` FourCC; readers agree
rows.note: Whole-film Pi: 15278169042 bytes, RF64, ds64 = {'riff_size': 15278169034, 'data_size': 15266291040, 'sample_count': 242322080, 'table': []}; ffprobe 242322080, bwf_info 242322080, ds64 sampleCount and the DAMF all give 242322080 frames; 0 container findings. Both size thresholds (data above 4 GiB; data below but RIFF above u32) promote to RF64 correctly (harness C22, C22b).

rows.internal: three verbatim Dolby segments + bed mask + LFE flags
rows.adm: required by Dolby validators; creator string gates acceptance
rows.classification: opaque; Dolby's validators accept the tagged file
rows.note: atmos_info 5.7.2 `--validate 1` and 1.1 accept oadec's ADM with `--dolby-origin-tag` (exit 0, no warnings) and refuse the default file on provenance only ('Content was not authored with Dolby tools'); bwf_info accepts both.

rows.classification: R is a writer defect on hypothetical input; 0 out-of-order events on every decoded stream
rows.note: C09: {'objects': 2, 'gaps': 0, 'overlaps': 1, 'starts_at_zero': True, 'ends_at_frames': True, 'last_end': 96000, 'overrun_objects': 0, 'blocks_shorter_than_interp': 0, 'tile_dec': {'50000': 1}, 'unsorted_objects': 0}. The writer never sorts; the CLI counts out-of-order events and reported 0 on every input of this audit.

rows.classification: flag silently ignored (unchanged since the previous audit)

rows.classification: silent lossy conversion
rows.note: None of ramp, gain, importance, 3-D size, ISF, bed events, non-48 kHz or out-of-order input produce a diagnostic; the only ADM-time failure is the unsupported bed channel (C14). Head cuts exit 7 for the truncated last access unit and the 96 kHz non-Atmos clip exits 2, both correctly.

rows.classification: tool validation
rows.note: 22 of 22 injected defects fired the intended detector with no specificity violation ([]); not testable on this material: ['M-A10'] (no inactive block in pi-head50m; covered by harness C16).

rows.classification: Dolby validators: accepted (tagged); EAR: accepted after the profile's stream-format edit; Dolby Atmos Renderer not available
rows.note: EAR speaker outputs of oadec's ADM and Dolby's Conversion-Tool ADM are sample-identical in 7 of 7 layout comparisons over ['fast-thd', 'pihead']. Dolby's DRP cannot open ADM or DAMF files, and no Dolby Atmos Renderer is installed, so section 26/27 rest on the Conversion Tool, DEE, atmos_info, bwf_info and EAR.

verdicts.Structural ADM verdict: MOSTLY VALID. Every default (bed-conformed, 48 kHz) file passes the container, reference-graph, chna and Dolby Atmos Master ADM profile v1.0 checks and Dolby's own validators (with the origin tag); `--no-bed-conform` object IDs and non-48 kHz programmes leave the profile without a warning.
verdicts.Atmos semantic fidelity verdict: MINOR SEMANTIC LOSS on every decoded stream tested: PCM, positions, timing and identity are exact and the file is functionally identical to Dolby's own DAMF-to-ADM conversion; the only loss on real material is the profile's fixed 250-sample ramp. For scenes the corpus does not contain (non-zero gain, ISF, 3-D size, bed events, importance) the output would be STRUCTURALLY VALID BUT SEMANTICALLY INCOMPLETE, and nothing tells the user.
